h: "The Faithful Guests Gather": Shemini Atzeres, Sum of the Festivals

p: It is brought in the holy Zohar
"On the eighth day it shall be an assembly for you"
"The faithful guests are with the King
and all of them gather with Him;
Yaakov is the head of the rejoicing,
it is brought concerning Shemini Atzeres
in which all the festivals are celebrated.
comes through the action of some mitzvah,
from the aspect of the seven holy attributes
However, on the day of Shemini Atzeres
there is no mitzvah in actual deed,
into the souls of Yisrael from Above
And it is like the holiness of Shabbos,
and this is the aspect of
"Yaakov is the head of the rejoicing,
that are called the faithful guests,
who are with the King always.
And on this he brings the pasuk,
"Fortunate are you, Yisrael; who is like you,
a people saved by Hashem" – precisely,
in which all festivals are celebrated;
for the eighth is the sum
for the bestowal of the seven holy attributes,
דְּהַיְינוּ יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח
Namely, the first Yom Tov of Pesach
corresponds to the attribute of Chesed,
And the seventh day of Pesach
corresponds to the aspect of Yosef HaTzaddik,
it saw the coffin of Yosef
Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
who conveyed the Torah to Yisrael,
for it is the time of the Giving of the Torah.
And the day of Rosh Hashanah,
corresponds to the Fear of Yitzchak,
David HaMelech, peace be upon him;
is to fast with affliction of the soul,
and this is the aspect of
David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
who raised up the yoke of teshuvah
is the aspect of the Cloud of Aharon.
corresponds to the aspect of Yaakov,
and this is that all the festivals
for there flow into it from Above
all the aspects of the bestowals of holiness
according to our words mentioned above.

inlineHeadings.text: The festival in which all are included
No mitzvah in deed, like Shabbos
The eighth, sum of seven festivals
The seventh of Pesach and Yosef

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 104b (Emor) — "'On the eighth day it shall be an assembly (atzeres) for you' (Bamidbar 29:35) — for this day is of the King alone, His joy with Israel. A parable of a king who invited guests, and all the members of his palace occupied themselves with them. Afterward the king said: Until now you and I occupied ourselves with the guests, and you offered offerings for the other nations every day; from now on, you and I will rejoice one day."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Bnei Yissaschar, Tishrei 13:5 — “The rejoicing of the Torah, and they rejoice on that day with the Torah — it appears to me according to the Zohar, Emor 104b: ‘Therefore it is written Atzeres, which is translated “gathering”; and on that day Yaakov is the head of the rejoicing, and all those guests rejoice with him; and so it is written, “Fortunate are you, Israel; who is like you,”’ and therefore on this day they read this parashah in the Torah; and it is written, ‘And He said to me: You are My servant, Israel, in whom I take glory.’ And since Yaakov is the attribute of truth, ‘Give truth to Yaakov’…” Connection: Bnei Yissaschar reads the same Zohar as the root of Simchas Torah and of reading Vezos HaBerachah, as Rav Tzadok does.

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 13, 29b — "Shemini Atzeres is a festival in its own right; on it is the welling forth of the Torah, to water the tree that is planted in the garden, and its roots and branches are like the circle (chug) of the earth, for all the festivals are celebrated in it."

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tehillim 114:4 — "'The sea saw and fled' (Tehillim 114:3): the sea saw Israel contending with one another to sanctify His Name… Another explanation: it saw the coffin of Yosef descending into the sea. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Let it flee before the one who fled, as it is written, 'and he fled and went outside' (Bereishis 39:12)."

paragraphs.text: Moed Katan 16b — "Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonasan: What is meant by 'The word of David son of Yishai, and the word of the man who was raised on high (hukam al)' (II Shmuel 23:1)? The word of David son of Yishai, who raised up the yoke (ullah) of teshuvah." Rashi: he repented first and opened the way for penitents.
